routes.text:
Privacy &
site information
Information about inquiry drafts, browser storage and the product details on this site.
Your inquiry
The form creates an email draft in your browser. It does not send your information to LZZ or upload drawings. To contact us, open the draft in your email app, add your attachments and send it yourself.
Saved drafts
The form saves your input and draft status in the current tab using sessionStorage, with a separate entry for each selected part. Your details stay available after a refresh but are not saved to an account or sent to LZZ. Select "Clear saved input" to remove the entry for the current part.
Your browser may restore this data when it restores a previous session. Clear your input before leaving a shared device. If browser storage is blocked or full, you can still use the form while the page is open. Select "Save draft" to download a text copy.
Cookies and external services
This site does not use analytics or advertising cookies. Your email provider, WhatsApp and other linked websites have their own privacy policies.
Product and company information
Product pages show a catalog image; the image is not an inspection record or a specification document. Original workshop photographs and company documents are identified separately from product examples.
Product pages use shorter titles and summaries of the catalog entries. The original names remain available on those pages, and the source material is kept in our archive. The summaries are not independently verified specifications for the photographed parts. Confirm material grades and tolerances with the team, along with the inspection and commercial terms for your order.
The engineering guides help you prepare an inquiry; they are not inspection records or customer case studies. They do not establish suitability for a particular application. Material filters help you find existing parts without creating duplicate product pages. English descriptions of company documents explain their contents but do not verify current validity.

Process comparison
CNC milling vs turning vs 5-axis machining: how to choose
On this page
Compare the processes by geometry
When does a part need more than one process?
Is 5-axis machining always more accurate?
What should I include when asking for a process recommendation?
A shaft or sleeve will usually start with turning. A housing with pockets and flat mounting faces is more likely to need milling. Angled features or access to several faces may call for a multi-axis setup. Some parts need a combination; send the drawing so we can review the sequence.
CNC turning operation; original LZZ process photograph.
CNC milling operation photographed in LZZ process materials; source folder dated December 2025.
Five-axis machining operation; original LZZ process photograph.
Compare the processes by geometry
Route to discuss
Geometry cues
Drawing and quote questions
CNC turning
Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis.
Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.
CNC milling
Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces.
Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.
Multi-axis machining
Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches.
Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.
CNC turning
Geometry cues
Rotational features such as a shaft, sleeve, disc or fitting, often arranged around an axis.
Drawing and quote questions
Define the datum axis, diameters, shoulders, grooves, threads and runout if required. Confirm whether cross-holes, flats or slots need secondary milling.
CNC milling
Geometry cues
Block-like or irregular forms with pockets, slots, holes, contours and planar mounting faces.
Drawing and quote questions
Define datum faces, pocket depth, hole patterns and positional relationships. Confirm stock, clamping surfaces, setups and inspection records.
Multi-axis machining
Geometry cues
Features distributed over several faces, angled faces or areas that need different tool approaches.
Drawing and quote questions
Define common datums, face-to-face and angular relationships. Review tool access, workholding and sequence against the model.
When does a part need more than one process?
A shaft with cross-holes, a turned fitting with milled flats or a housing with angled faces may need more than one operation or setup. The route should preserve the relationships between critical features. Send a 3D model and controlled 2D drawing so the team can review datums, access and inspection together.
Is 5-axis machining always more accurate?
No single process label guarantees accuracy. Acceptance depends on the part geometry, machine and setup, datum strategy, material, finishing and measurement method. If an interface matters, state its tolerance and datum on the drawing and ask how it will be produced and checked. Any tolerance target needs feature-specific review.
What should I include when asking for a process recommendation?
A 3D model and the controlling 2D drawing revision.
Material grade and condition, or the functional requirement if still undecided.
Quantity for the first order and expected repeat pattern, if known.
Critical datums, fits, surface requirements and required inspection records.
Finish, packaging and required arrival date, with any standards or approvals identified.

Manufacturing guide
Planning CNC parts for prototypes and repeat orders
On this page
Identify the working surfaces
Specify critical dimensions

Identify the working surfaces
For a housing or shaft, the surfaces that meet other parts matter as much as the outside shape. The same applies to a mounting block. Mark the surfaces that locate, seal, slide or carry load on the drawing so you can discuss tolerances in relation to their function.
Compare
milled pockets and housings
with
turned shafts and fittings
. Some designs need both operations; the geometry determines the process choice.
Specify critical dimensions
Give the datums and mating details for critical features, with their acceptance limits. A 3D model shows the shape but may leave fits or surface texture undefined. It may also omit edge conditions and measurement methods. Include a controlled 2D drawing when these requirements apply.
Tolerances need review against the specific drawing. The material and feature geometry affect the assessment, as do the setup and measurement method; a single tolerance cannot apply to every catalog part. Agree on
inspection requirements and supporting records
for your design.
Specify material and finish
State the exact alloy or plastic grade and any material-certificate requirement. For coated parts, specify the finish and whether critical dimensions apply before or after treatment. Mark areas that need masking, cosmetic faces and burr-sensitive edges.
The
material and finish checklist
covers these details. Catalog photographs show shapes and surfaces; they cannot establish a coating specification or provide material certification.
Agree on prototype checks
Explain the purpose of the prototype. You may need to check assembly fit and access, assess appearance or run a functional test. Agree on the checks needed for revision or approval. If the design changes, issue a revised drawing with the affected dimensions identified; an email description alone is not enough.
The
prototype machining examples
show trial parts. When requesting a quote, separate the trial quantity from expected repeat orders. Orders start at 1 piece. Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing; transit is additional. Confirm price and inspection requirements for your project.
Confirm repeat-order requirements
Use the approved drawing revision and confirm the material and finish. Agree on the inspection scope and packaging requirements before ordering. If you need a first-article report or material documents, confirm their format and availability. Sample approval does not cover a changed design or material.

routes.text:

Answers before

Custom CNC machining FAQ
Practical answers about ordering custom CNC parts, preparing drawings, inspection and shipping, so you can get a qualified quotation.

Quotes & ordering
01
What is the minimum order quantity?
Orders start at 1 piece. Include your first-order quantity and expected repeat quantities so the quotation can distinguish prototype work from future batches.
02
What is the production lead time?
Production takes 7–14 business days after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing. Shipping time is additional. Record the confirmed production schedule and delivery arrangements in your quotation and order.
Preparing a quotation
03
What should I send for a quotation?
Please provide the following information:
Drawing revision and units
Exact material grade and condition
Finish and surface treatment
First-order and expected repeat quantities
Delivery destination
STEP model, where available
Dimensioned 2D drawing with critical tolerances, threads and acceptance requirements
04
Does the website send my inquiry or upload my drawing?
No. The inquiry form prepares an email draft. Check the draft, open it in your email application, attach your drawings and send it there. Copy and download options are also available; preparing a draft does not send an inquiry to LZZ.
Prepare RFQ email
Processes & specifications
05
Which machining services can I discuss with LZZ?
Our five service areas are CNC milling, CNC turning, five-axis CNC machining, plastic machining and casting machining. Share the complete part geometry so the route, workholding and finishing requirements can be reviewed together. For castings, agree who supplies and approves the blank.
06
How should I specify the material and finish?
Specify the exact material grade and condition, not just aluminum, steel or plastic. Identify cosmetic faces, surface treatment requirements, masking and dimensions that must be checked after finishing. The quotation should record the agreed specification.
07
Can every feature hold ±0.01 mm?
No. ±0.01 mm is a conditional engineering reference for selected critical features after review, not a general part tolerance or guarantee. Material, geometry, setup and measurement method determine whether it applies. Identify each critical feature on the drawing for confirmation.
Inspection & delivery
08
Which inspection documents should I request?
Specify the required dimensional results, first-article records, material traceability and finishing documents before ordering. Agree the features, sampling and report format. The quotation records the included document package and any additional cost; request current calibration evidence separately where needed.
09
Is LZZ ISO 9001 certified?
LZZ is ISO 9001 certified. For supplier qualification, request the current certificate for Hangzhou Lizhizao Precision Machinery Co., Ltd., including its number, issuer, validity, scope and verification details. Company awards are separate from the ISO certificate, and quality-system certification does not replace part-specific acceptance or industry approval.
10
How are packing and international shipping agreed?
Provide the destination, receiving requirements and any vulnerable or cosmetic surfaces that need protection. Confirm the packing method, transport method, trade term and named place in the quotation. Agree the packing list, commercial invoice and other required documents. Transit time is separate from production time.
Case studies & further resources
11
What do the machining case studies demonstrate?
The studies use original LZZ workshop photographs to discuss visible part features, machining sequences and drawing questions. They are not customer performance reports, inspection results or proof of a particular delivery outcome.

Finishing services and acceptance points
We support deburring, bead blasting, polishing, anodizing, passivation and plating as appropriate to the selected material. The quotation defines the finish and any accompanying documents; not every treatment is suitable for every alloy.
Deburring and polishing: specify edge breaks, cosmetic faces and any controlled roughness.
Bead blasting: agree appearance, protected interfaces and whether a reference sample is needed.
Anodizing: specify alloy, color, coating requirements and masked threads or mating surfaces.
Passivation and plating: identify the applicable material, process specification, protected areas and acceptance documents.

Production planning
One sample asks
a question.
A repeat order needs
an approved answer.
A prototype helps you check the design before ordering more parts. For a repeat batch, use the approved drawing revision and confirm the material and finish. You also need an agreed inspection plan and delivery terms. The quantity that makes a small batch economical depends on the part and its setup, not a fixed industry threshold.
AI-generated illustration — not an LZZ order or production record.
Validate
Check fit, function or appearance with a first sample.
Approve
Lock the drawing, material and finish with agreed inspection.
Repeat
Carry the approved specification into controlled production.
01
Validate
the first sample
Agree what the sample must prove: assembly fit, a critical interface, operation or appearance. Define the checks needed for sample acceptance before moving to a repeat order.
Drawing questions
Use the sample to identify design questions related to fit, function or appearance.
Workholding and access
Review workholding and tool access while confirming the design.
Material, finish and acceptance
Check the specified grade, condition and final appearance. Define fit, function and sample acceptance checks. Confirm the prototype price and schedule for the specific part.
02
Approve what
will repeat
For a repeat order, release one controlled drawing revision and carry the approved material and finish into the quotation. Agree the acceptance plan and the documents to accompany delivery.
A repeat batch uses a controlled revision with agreed material, finish and inspection.
Specification to carry forward
Agree revision approval and how changed features are identified.
Confirm material documents and the finish standard, including masking and dimensions after treatment.
Retain the approved specification unless a change is agreed.
Evidence to agree
Define batch sampling and critical-feature records.
Confirm the measurement method, instrument evidence and available report format.
Agree the acceptance plan and delivery documents.
If the drawing changes, pause and confirm the impact. The old sample may no longer represent the new revision.
03
Plan the
repeat order
Confirm the setup and machining sequence for the released revision, including critical datums, and whether the route changes with quantity. Request a new quote for the batch quantity and price, and confirm the production slot.
There is no fixed quantity threshold for an economical small batch.
Economics depend on the part geometry and its setup.
Minimum order
1 piece
Production lead time
7–14 business days
after drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing.
Shipping time is additional.
Share the part, quantity and required arrival date so we can quote price and delivery arrangements.

What to include in your next batch RFQ
Share the drawing, first-order quantity, expected repeat pattern and required arrival date. Identify critical dimensions and records, then confirm price, production slot, inspection evidence, finish, packing and shipping terms for that order. The
ordering guide
explains the information to agree before shipment.
Compare suppliers before committing
Compare the quoted scope, not headline unit price alone. Use the same drawing revision, material and finish, and check the following points with each supplier.
Same specification
Make sure each quote uses the same drawing revision, material and finish.
What is included
Check setup, inspection records, packaging and delivery basis are stated.
Exclusions or substitutions
Confirm that any exclusions or substitutions are clear.
Changes and repeat orders
Ask how changes, nonconforming parts and repeat orders will be handled.

RFQ Checklist
The drawing defines the part.
Your brief defines the quote.
Accurate drawings and clear requirements help us review your part and prepare a quote.
Use this checklist to prepare the information we need before sending your request.
AI-generated illustration — not an LZZ order or inspection record.
Five essential requirements
for a complete RFQ
Drawing revision
3D model and 2D drawing when needed, part number, units and revision.
Material & finish
Exact material or functional requirement, finish details and applicable standards.
Acceptance criteria
Critical dimensions, datums, tolerances and inspection requirements.
Quantity
Initial quantity and expected repeat pattern.
Delivery
Arrival date, packaging, shipping basis and relevant customs requirements.
Download order acceptance checklist
A buyer worksheet to record drawing revision, critical features, documents and shipping requirements.
Define how the part will be accepted
Use a consistent drawing package and agree the inspection requirements before ordering.
Send a consistent drawing package
Include a 3D model, such as STEP, and a 2D drawing when dimensions, fits or surface requirements are not fully defined in the model. Label the part number, units and drawing revision. If the files disagree, identify which document controls before requesting a quotation.
For multi-axis parts, include the overall envelope, stock dimensions and part weight where known so tool access and setup can be reviewed.
Only have a sample?
For an existing sample without a drawing, explain what is known and ask what additional measurement or design work would be needed. A sample alone cannot establish hidden material or treatment requirements.
Mark the dimensions used for acceptance
Identify mating bores and shaft fits on the drawing, with their datums and tolerances. Mark sealing faces, threads and any other critical features too. State whether dimensions apply before or after finishing.
If you need a particular inspection record, send the format or an example with your inquiry. Agree on inspection and documentation requirements before ordering, and ask LZZ to confirm the measurement method, instrument range, calibration evidence and availability of any project-specific records required for your part.
Inspection & documentation requirements
Specify the material and final surface
Define the material, finish and applicable standards on your drawing or in your RFQ notes.
Material requirements
State the exact alloy or polymer grade, or the functional requirement if selection is still open. Include any required material documentation and whether substitutes may be considered.
Finish and surface requirements
Provide the finish specification, appearance, cosmetic faces, masking and edge conditions. Include any customer or industry standards and certificates required for this part or program. State the required standard, revision and scope.
A material or capability category on this site does not establish industry certification or application compliance. The
material and finish checklist
explains the decisions behind these fields.
What drawing review returns
Our quotation brings together the proposed process, material, finishing, order quantity, inspection documents, production schedule and shipping basis. Where geometry or acceptance requirements need clarification, we identify the open points before you approve production.
Use the
order acceptance checklist
to record the drawing revision, critical features, documents and shipping requirements in one place. This is a buyer worksheet, not an inspection report.
Set the commercial brief
Provide quantity, delivery and commercial details so we can confirm the scope and timing in your quotation.
Minimum order
1 piece
Production lead time
7–14 business days
After drawing and order confirmation, including surface finishing.
Transit time is additional.
Initial quantity
Quantity per part number.
Repeat pattern
Expected repeat orders, if known.
Delivery details
Required arrival date and postcode.
Packaging
Any special packaging requirements.
Shipping basis
Incoterm and customs, duties or taxes responsibilities.
Response deadline
Your decision or response deadline, if applicable.
Please confirm all details in your quotation.
Ready to prepare the email?
If your project needs an NDA or a controlled transfer method, contact LZZ before sending restricted files. This website does not automatically create an NDA.
